title: Unencrypted GPS Transmission
description: Child's device (EE2) transmits live GPS coordinates to the backend (P1) without encryption, exposing sensitive location data.
assumptions: Device capabilities and network security posture are assumed sufficient to transmit raw GPS data.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: Backend (P1) receives and stores the unencrypted GPS coordinates from the child device (EE2), creating a data flow where sensitive location data is processed and potentially stored.
assumptions: Backend system is assumed to have appropriate security controls to prevent unauthorized access or leakage.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The backend process (P1) writes location pings to the Location History Store (DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data (location pings) to a data store, which is a boundary crossing. This is an explicit disclosure intended by design.
assumptions: The location pings contain personal data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Location History Store (DS1) receives data from the backend process (P1). This is a data disclosure as the store receives personal data from a process, crossing the boundary between the process and the data store.
assumptions: The data received from P1 is personal data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) forwards new location pings to the Geofencing Engine (P2). This constitutes a data disclosure as P1 transfers personal location data to a third-party process (P2) without explicit consent or a direct data store intermediary, violating the minimality principle.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) receives location pings from the Backend (P1). This is a data disclosure as P2 processes personal location data from a third-party process (P1) without explicit consent or a direct data store intermediary, violating the minimality principle.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: A malicious actor could potentially access the Family Account Store (DS2) and extract the configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) intended for the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). This constitutes a Low severity threat where the data store is the originator of the flow.
assumptions: The Family Account Store contains sensitive user location preferences and zone configurations.

title: Unauthorized Access to Family Account Data
description: A malicious actor could potentially access the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) and extract the configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) intended for the Family Account Store (DS2). This constitutes a High severity threat where the process is the originator of the flow.
assumptions: The Geofencing & Alert Engine has access to the Family Account Store's zone definitions.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: An external entity (EE1) may attempt to access or manipulate the geofencing data flow (P2) without proper authorization, potentially exposing sensitive location information.
assumptions: The system allows external entities to interact with the process without explicit permission checks.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific threat type 'L' (Unauthorized Access) is the most appropriate classification for this interaction type, as the context suggests a push notification mechanism rather than a direct data retrieval or modification flow.

title: Data Exfiltration Risk
description: The parent external entity (EE1) may exfiltrate or leak the arrival/departure notifications pushed by the child process (P2) to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The notification mechanism is not secured with encryption or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the threat type 'D' (Data Exfiltration) is the most appropriate classification, as the context suggests a push notification mechanism rather than a direct data retrieval or modification flow.

title: Data Leakage
description: Parent (ExternalEntity) registers an account, creating a child profile (name, DOB, school) and defining geofence zones. This flow involves the transfer of sensitive personal data (PII) from an external entity to a process, which is a valid interaction type. The threat type L (Leakage) is appropriate for data that is exposed or transmitted without proper authorization or encryption.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE1) has access to the data and is transmitting it to the backend process (P1).

title: Intrusion
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process) receives the account registration and profile data. This flow involves the transfer of sensitive personal data (PII) from an external entity to a process, which is a valid interaction type. The threat type I (Intrusion) is appropriate for unauthorized access or interception of data during transmission.
assumptions: The backend process (P1) is receiving the data from the parent entity (EE1).

title: Data Disclosure
description: The backend process (P1) transfers account, child profile, and geofence zone data to the Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process is transferring personal data across a boundary to a data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data store (DS2) receives data from the backend process (P1) and stores it. This is a data disclosure as the store is receiving personal data across a boundary.

title: Unauthorized Location Access
description: Parent (ExternalEntity) requests to view child's current location or history on a map without explicit consent or authorization.
assumptions: Parent entity has access to the map data but lacks the specific permission to retrieve location details.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Process P1 (Mobile App Backend) discloses sensitive location data (current location or history) to the Parent (ExternalEntity) without a secure, authenticated channel.
assumptions: The backend process is exposed to the external entity's request.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) accesses stored location history (DS1) without explicit authorization or encryption, potentially exposing sensitive user location data.
assumptions: Assumption: The backend application has the necessary permissions to read the data store.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain: The specific authorization model for the backend access is not fully detailed in the provided context.

title: Inappropriate Data Exposure
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) exposes location history data to an external entity (the parent's map/history view) without proper data masking or filtering, violating the principle of least privilege.
assumptions: Assumption: The parent's view is not configured with data masking capabilities.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain: The specific data masking configuration for the parent's view is not detailed in the provided context.

title: Unauthorized Location Sharing
description: Parent (EE1) initiates a data flow to a Process (P1) to share location data with a secondary guardian. This action is triggered by the parent's intent to invite a relative, creating a privacy risk where the parent's location data is transmitted to an external party (the guardian) without the child's explicit consent.
assumptions: The parent has the authority to invite a secondary guardian to view the child's location.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app backend (P1) processes the incoming request to share the child's location with a secondary guardian. This action triggers the disclosure of the child's location data to an external entity (the guardian), which may be processed or stored in a way that compromises the child's privacy.
assumptions: The mobile app backend has the capability to share location data with external parties.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child's Location
description: Process P1 grants access to the child's live location to ExternalEntity EE3, which is not authorized to view this sensitive personal data.
assumptions: The secondary guardian (EE3) is not a trusted party with explicit permission to access the child's live location.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing
description: ExternalEntity EE3 shares the child's live location with Process P1, which is an invalid interaction as external entities do not have modeled flows between each other.
assumptions: The sharing of live location data between an external entity and a process is not a valid LINDDUN interaction.

title: Data Leakage
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are shared with an external advertising/analytics partner, potentially exposing sensitive user data.
assumptions: The partner has access to the raw or aggregated data flows.

title: Data Leakage
description: The advertising/analytics partner may access or misuse the shared aggregated usage and engagement analytics.
assumptions: The partner has access to the data flows.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Child (ExternalEntity) sends a manual check-in / SOS message with their current location to the parent (Process). This message is attributed to the user (EE2) and constitutes non-repudiable data evidence of their location.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and stored.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process) receives and stores a manual check-in / SOS message with the Child's current location. This data is attributed to the user (EE2) and constitutes non-repudiable data evidence of their location.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and stored.
